title: Zenzap raises $44M for its AI chat app that aims to replace WhatsApp in the workplace
key_facts: Zenzap, a private work messenger with built-in AI, raised $44 million.
Investors include Bessemer, Lightspeed and The Garage, plus Wix president Nir Zohar and Yoram Tietz, former GM of EY.
Founder Guy Weiss started the company in 2022 and had bootstrapped it before raising money for the first time.
Clients named include FedEx, Dollar General, Taco Bell and Starbucks; branches of IHOP and McDonald's use it to coordinate shifts.
Paid plans start at $51 a month for up to 20 users; AI agents use credit-based pricing.
The company has 50 staff in the US, Tel Aviv and Europe and plans to hire in product and research.
quote_evidence: The company has raised $44 million in funding from investors including Bessemer, Lightspeed, and The Garage.
"You can't use WhatsApp or iMessage within a workplace with the AI agent on top of it because it doesn't comply with IT."
why_it_matters_hint: Targets workers who run their jobs on personal chat apps, a group far bigger than office desk staff.
